questions.q: How was the Water Rat feeling at the start of the chapter?
choices: Restless, without knowing why
Happy, lazy and quite content
Angry with Toad for his boasting
Sick in bed with a bad cold
questions.evidence: The Water Rat was restless, and he did not exactly know why.

questions.q: What season is beginning in this chapter, causing so many creatures to leave?
choices: The end of summer, as autumn approaches
Early spring, as the first flowers open
The middle of a long, cold winter
The first warm days of early summer
questions.evidence: a feeling in the air of change and departure

questions.q: The author compares nature to a "Grand Hotel" whose guests "pack, pay, and depart." What does this comparison show?
choices: That many creatures leave as the season ends, like guests
That the animals must pay money to live in the fields and woods
That the Rat wants to build a hotel by the river
That the river is crowded with tourists and boats
questions.evidence: Nature's Grand Hotel has its Season

questions.q: What were the field-mice busy doing when Rat visited the wheat field?
choices: Packing up and moving to winter quarters
Having a picnic at the edge of the field
Harvesting the wheat for the farmer
Building a little boat to sail away in
questions.evidence: others were already elbow-deep packing their belongings

questions.q: Why did the field-mice say they had to move out early?
choices: Before the harvest machines came clicking round
Because the river was rising and flooding the field
Because weasels from the Wild Wood were coming
Because the Rat had told them it was time to go
questions.evidence: before those horrid machines begin clicking round the fields

questions.q: What happened as Rat turned to leave the field-mice?
choices: He tripped over a hat-box and fell
He stayed to help them pack their things
He invited them all home to dinner
He found a little lost mouse in the wheat
questions.evidence: tripped over a hat-box, and fell

questions.q: What happened to the swallow who once tried "stopping on" for the winter?
choices: The cold, dark days were so bad it flew south in the snow
It nearly froze and had to be rescued and warmed by the Rat
It loved the winter so much that it stayed for good
It moved into the Rat's snug house until spring

questions.q: How did listening to the swallows affect Rat?
choices: It woke a wild new longing in him for the South
It made him glad that he could stay at home
It made him angry, and he chased them away
It made him so sleepy that he nodded off

questions.q: What did the swallows say draws them back home each spring?
choices: Another call, for English meadows, orchards and streams
The Rat's kind invitations to come and stay by the river
Fear of the hunters who trap birds in the South
The bad food and cold winds of the Southern lands
questions.evidence: the other call is not for us too, in its due season

questions.q: Who sat down beside Rat by the dusty lane?
choices: A travelling Sea Rat
The Mole, back from a walk
A tired swallow
Toad in a disguise
questions.evidence: I'm a seafaring rat, I am

questions.q: What city did the Sea Rat say he originally came from?
choices: Constantinople
Venice
Alexandria
Marseilles
questions.evidence: the port I originally hail from is Constantinople

questions.q: Why had the Sea Rat left the farm where he had been living for six months?
choices: He felt the old call of the sea and the South
The farmer had caught him in the barn and thrown him out
The farm burned down one night in the summer
He was looking for his lost family along the road
questions.evidence: following the old call, back to the old life

questions.q: When the Sea Rat winks and says "The captain's cabin's good enough for me," what is he hinting?
choices: He travels in comfort and skips the crew's hard work
He is secretly the captain of the ship himself
He sleeps down in the hot, stuffy hold with cargo
He has never actually been on a ship at all
questions.evidence: The captain's cabin's good enough for me.

questions.q: What did the Rat bring back for the Sea Rat's meal?
choices: French bread, garlic sausage, cheese and wine
Cold chicken, potted ham, and a bottle of lemonade
Shell-fish from the river and some brown bread
Only a crust of dry bread and a cup of water
questions.evidence: a yard of long French bread

questions.q: Rat said his life felt "narrow and circumscribed." What does "circumscribed" mean?
choices: Limited, with fixed boundaries
Exciting and full of travel
Round, like a circle
Written down very carefully

questions.q: What did Rat do after the Sea Rat walked away down the road?
choices: Packed a satchel and set off to go South
Fell fast asleep in the hedge by the lane
Ran straight to tell the Badger all about it
Went out fishing on the river to forget
questions.evidence: Going South, with the rest of them

questions.q: What made the Mole realize something was badly wrong with Rat?
choices: Rat's eyes had turned a strange, shifting grey
Rat was shouting angrily at everyone on the road
Rat had a high fever and was shivering
Rat refused to speak a single word to him
questions.evidence: not his friend's eyes, but the eyes of some other animal

questions.q: How did the Mole help Rat recover at the end of the chapter?
choices: He talked of harvest and winter, then gave him paper for poems
He took him on a long journey down the river to the sea
He ran to fetch a doctor and some medicine from the village
He scolded him sharply for being so foolish
questions.evidence: It's quite a long time since you did any poetry

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Rat longs to travel South until Mole helps him settle again
Toad escapes from prison dressed as a washerwoman
Mole visits his old home and the field-mice come carol-singing
The animals fight the weasels to win back Toad Hall
questions.evidence: the cure had at least begun
